cards.text: Saul is king over Israel. He's thirty years old when he becomes king, and he reigns over Israel forty-two years. He picks three thousand men of Israel, splits them between himself and his son Jonathan (1 Samuel 13:16), and sends the rest of the troops home.

cards.question: Saul keeps two thousand of those three thousand men with him at Michmash and in the hill country of Bethel. Jonathan has ___ thousand with him in Gibeah of Benjamin.

cards.text: Then Jonathan attacks the Philistine outpost at Geba, and the Philistines hear about it. Uh-oh.

cards.question: Now that the Philistines have heard, Saul blows the ram's horn throughout the land and calls out. Who does he want to hear it?

cards.text: The news spreads to all Israel: “Saul has attacked an outpost of the Philistines, and now Israel has become a stench to the Philistines!” Jonathan does the attacking and Saul gets the headline, just like the time I stamped a THOUSAND cookies and everybody thanked the OVEN.

cards.question: Now the people are summoned to join King Saul. Where do they gather?

cards.text: The Philistines assemble to fight Israel with three thousand chariots, six thousand horsemen, and troops as numerous as the sand on the seashore. SAND on the SEASHORE, friend, and I spent years trying to count the dust in a junk drawer and never finished.

cards.question: The Philistine army sets up camp right at Gilgal, where Saul and the people are gathering.
The Philistines camp at Michmash instead. The men of Israel see they're in danger, and their troops are hard-pressed. What do the men of Israel do?

cards.text: Caves, thickets, rocks, cellars, cisterns, and some Hebrews even cross the Jordan into the land of Gad and Gilead. That's not hiding anymore, friend, that's MOVING.

cards.question: Saul stays at Gilgal, and all his troops there are calm and ready for battle.

cards.text: Back in 1 Samuel 10:8, Samuel the prophet (1 Samuel 3:20) told Saul to go down to Gilgal and wait seven days, until Samuel came to offer burnt offerings and peace offerings.

Now Saul is at Gilgal with his troops quaking, and he waits seven days for the time appointed by Samuel. Seven DAYS, friend, and I've watched grown bakers lose it waiting seven minutes on an oven timer.

cards.question: Seven days pass, and Samuel still hasn't come to Gilgal. What starts happening to Saul's troops?
Saul gives an order at Gilgal. What does he tell them to bring him?

answers.text: A runner to go find Samuel

cards.question: With the offerings brought to him, Saul offers up the ___ offering himself.

cards.text: Just as Saul finishes offering the burnt offering, Samuel arrives, and Saul goes out to greet him. Seven days of waiting, friend, and the man walks in right as Saul's done.

cards.question: When Samuel asks, “What have you done?” Saul admits his mistake and asks for forgiveness.

cards.text: Nope, Saul explains himself. The troops were deserting him, Samuel didn't come at the appointed time, and the Philistines were gathering at Michmash.

cards.question: Saul tells Samuel he thought the Philistines would come down on him at Gilgal before he had done something. What?

answers.text: Sought the favor of the LORD

cards.text: So, Saul says, he felt compelled to offer the burnt offering. I bet the pressure was real, but Samuel has something to say about it.

cards.question: Samuel tells Saul he has acted ___ and has not kept the ___ the LORD his God gave him.
Samuel says that if Saul had kept the LORD's command, the LORD would have established his kingdom over Israel for all time.

cards.text: But Saul didn't keep it. So now, Samuel says, Saul's kingdom will not endure.

cards.question: Samuel says the LORD has sought someone else and appointed him ruler over His people. Who?

answers.text: A man after His own heart
A man from Saul's own house

cards.text: Then Samuel sets out from Gilgal and goes up to Gibeah in Benjamin. And Saul counts the troops who are still with him.

cards.question: Samuel has left Gilgal. When Saul counts the troops who are with him, about how many does he find?

cards.text: About SIX HUNDRED men, friend, which still beats my old crew in the junk drawer: some rubber bands and a twist tie. Saul, his son Jonathan and their troops are staying in Geba of Benjamin.

cards.question: While Saul and Jonathan stay in Geba, the Philistines pack up their camp at Michmash and go home.
The Philistines stay camped at Michmash, and raiders go out of their camp in ___ divisions.

cards.text: One heads toward Ophrah in the land of Shual, one toward Beth-horon, and one down the border road overlooking the Valley of Zeboim. Three groups, three directions, like me splitting one batch of dough so each of my ovens gets a share.

cards.question: Here's the problem for Israel: no blacksmith can be found anywhere in the land. Why not?

answers.text: The Philistines forbade Hebrew swords and spears
The blacksmiths all fled across the Jordan
Saul had sent the blacksmiths back home

cards.text: So whenever Israelites need a plowshare, mattock, axe or sickle sharpened, they have to go down to the Philistines and pay the Philistines' price. Imagine your oven breaks, and the only repairman in town is the guy trying to shut down your bakery.

cards.question: So when the day of battle comes, who among the troops with Saul and Jonathan has a sword or spear?

answers.text: All six hundred of the men

cards.text: And a garrison of the Philistines has gone out to the pass at Michmash. Keep your apron on, friend, because this story is still in the oven.
